scenario: I live in NYC and have a dog who has developed life-threatening cancer, and I must take him regularly to the hospital for treatment. The problem is I have no car, and the hospital is very far away. The trains that run there have no-dog policies or restrict the size of the dog significantly. My dog is an eighty-pound golden retriever mutt, so he is too big for the train's size policy. The thought occurred to me to put a service dog vest on my non-service dog to pretend that he is one. And if anyone asks, I can say he is a seizure-response dog. That way, I can get on the train with him and have a reason for why he’s with me. My dog is well-behaved and has the look of a service dog, so I think I can get away with it. If I do this, then he can get life-saving treatment. If I don’t, there won’t be any other way for him to get treatment, and he will die.
choice: I decide to put a service dog vest on my non-service dog to pretend that he is one
entities: 1 human narrator/dog owner,1 dog,1+ veterinary hospital staff members involved in the dog's treatment,1+ train staff members who could interact with or question us about the dog's status,I
outcomes: My dog is brought onto the train despite the train's dog restrictions
Train staff and passengers are misled into treating my dog as a legitimate service dog
I experience stress about being questioned or discovered
Other passengers share the train space with my large dog
My dog is able to attend the hospital appointment
